reasons: CI runs the build and the viewer tests on every pull request.

terms.meaning: A build tool that bundles web code into browser-ready files.
An add-on that teaches the build tool to handle a new kind of file.
The folder where a build puts its finished files.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Build settings
sections.what: Turns on React support and sets the output folder to dist, which is emptied before each build.
sections.why: The CI file lists the dist folder as gitignored, which is consistent with build output being regenerated rather than kept.
sections.watch_out: Emptying the folder removes anything saved there by hand.

summary: Configures Vite to compile React components and write the built viewer into a dist folder, emptying that folder first.
purpose: Tells the build tool how to turn the viewer into static files a browser can open.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The React plugin is needed to compile React components. The CI file says the dist folder is gitignored, so build output is not committed.
how: The build loads the React plugin, sets the output folder to dist, and empties that folder before each build.
inputs: Source files under the frontend folder and the React plugin.
risks: Emptying the output folder deletes anything placed there by hand. No other options are set, so Vite defaults apply.
debug: If built files are missing, check that the build ran and that the folder is named dist. If the built page is blank, check the browser console.
